qd6a1430f.question: A Task head is written in draft status by createFromPlan (contract postcondition), but a Task whose edit 'returns to draft' and 'needs re-approval' (ac21) and whose build is admitted by the plan's approval must start approved. Resolve: after writing each head, createFromPlan applies the approve operation through LifecycleService.apply as the plan's approving actor, so a new Task is approved on the plan's approval and an edit later returns it to draft (recommended), or leave new Tasks in draft and add a separate Task approval step before build (a change to the build admission gate).

summary.prose: When a plan is approved, each of its Tasks becomes an artifact of its own, with its own id, revision, status, change log, feedback and issue, and the Story's Tasks sit together under one Tasks file that also hands out the next Task number. A person can refine a Task's wording, size, checks or tests without redoing the plan; the Task returns to draft and needs the local user's approval again, and the plan keeps its revision. Adding, dropping or reordering Tasks, or changing what depends on what, is refused with a pointer to a re-plan, and when a re-plan is approved the Tasks are brought into line without ever reusing an id. A Task's build rounds are written to its own history and it completes when a round passes the gate.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Chosen framework (a1): a shared artifact envelope with typed payloads, stored as a head file plus two append-only sidecar files whose lines carry the owning artifact id, behind a single identity module, with one upfront conversion and no compatibility code. The envelope carries identity, description, parent, references, a typed lifecycle (revision, approval, review, signoffs, staleness, status) and a tracker binding or attachments; the change log and feedback are separate append-only line files; each existing artifact type shrinks to a payload codec and a renderer. Tracker comment reading and attaching are added to the port and implemented for the GitHub adapter only.

ownedContracts.name: TaskSet
ownedContracts.purpose: The Tasks file of a plan: the Task artifacts, their ids, and how a re-plan is brought into line without reusing an id.

consumedContracts.name: ArtifactIdScheme
consumedContracts.purpose: The single place artifact ids are made and recognised: the existing hierarchical typed ids extended for Epic, Story, Task, the Tasks file and diagrams, one story and task form, the folder-name date source, and the functional-requirement id helpers that live in id.ts today.

consumedContracts.name: ArtifactEnvelope
consumedContracts.purpose: The common shape of every stored entity and the one reader and writer for it, with References and namespaced Actors.

consumedContracts.name: HistoryRecords
consumedContracts.purpose: The change log entry and the Feedback entry shapes, the persisted sidecar record that carries the owning artifact id, and the append and read API, including how an update says which feedback it addressed.

consumedContracts.name: Lifecycle
consumedContracts.purpose: The typed lifecycle structures, the ten statuses and their transitions, the revision and content-hash rule, the completion roll-up and the conflict check against the log tail.

consumedContracts.name: TrackerBinding
consumedContracts.purpose: The typed binding between a lifecycle artifact and its tracker issue, the attachments of supporting artifacts, and the tracker port operations to read comments and attach, implemented for the GitHub adapter.

boundary.internal: Task artifacts: creation of the Tasks file and the Task issues at plan approval, direct edits of a Task's own content with local re-approval, refusal of structural edits, and the re-plan reconciliation. Private to this Story are the diff of a Task against the new plan and the build-round recording in a Task's history.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The id module and its removal of the second scheme: the folder-name formatter moved into the path scheme, the date source fixed to the epic's creation time, the functional-requirement id helpers and their callers moved with stored FR ids staying valid, issue titles switched to the artifact id, and the delivery module's ordinals. The old issue-body marker is not read. Private to this Story are the exact text of the issue title and the relocation of the helpers.

The envelope model, the one reader and writer, the History API and the sidecar record shape as a contract, and the repository version marker. Private to this Story are the head-file schema, the per-type payload codec registry and how the old per-type read functions delegate to the reader.

The lifecycle rules: status transitions, the revision and content-hash computation, the staleness record, the completion roll-up and the integrity check against the log tail on approve, review and complete. Private to this Story are the hash canonicalisation and how a roll-up is cached or recomputed.

The physical sidecar storage: file layout, the merge attributes for the line files, per-artifact filtering, read-time ordering and de-duplication, and the write order of log entry before head with the repair of a log that is ahead of its head. Private to this Story are the line format and the file naming beside a head.

People-facing feedback: adding feedback and replies from a client, listing open feedback, the addresses rule at revision time, and the per-user identity declaration with alias linking. Private to this Story are the identity file format and the display of linked identities.

The typed binding and attachments, the tracker port additions implemented for GitHub, the retry of pending links and posts, and the switch of unit-issue bookkeeping to the binding. Private to this Story are the permalink construction and the retry bookkeeping.

Comment sync: reading human comments into feedback at implement, validate or on request, classifying a revision request or a suggestion from the first line, and posting feedback once. Private to this Story are the first-line commands, the derived since point and the filter for the framework's own posts.

The conversion command: previews, repeats, back-fills history, renames standalone S001 to s1 rewriting the references it can with no alias, creates Epic, Story and Task artifacts for what exists, verifies through the delivery reader, and sets the repository version. Private to this Story are the per-type conversion mappings and the verification report.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase D — Tasks and tracker comment sync

nonFunctional.performance: Reading an artifact reads its head; the log tail is read only on approve, review and complete, and counts, open feedback and status are computed on read. The delivery loader still reads each artifact once. Loading a repository of about a thousand artifacts must stay within twice today's load time on the same machine.
nonFunctional.security: Gates use the live tracker identity only; declared aliases are never trusted for a decision. The identity file is local and read for attribution. Tracker comments are read through the existing gh path of the GitHub adapter, with no new credential and no direct REST call.
nonFunctional.observability: Every state change appends a change log entry with actor, operation and, where relevant, revision and status; a conflict, a log-ahead-of-head repair, a failed attach and a pending link are logged and surfaced in the unit's result, not hidden.
nonFunctional.durability: Heads are replaced atomically as today; sidecar lines are append-only and de-duplicated by (artifactId, entry id) so a repeated append is harmless; a write appends its log entry before it replaces the head so a failure between the two leaves a detectable, repairable gap; the conversion is one commit, repeatable, and reverts with one git revert.

Reads the Task's own build rounds instead of the BUILD record's per-task results; the BUILD record keeps its results for the delivery view.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Owns TaskPayload, TaskSet, createFromPlan, reconcile and edit as sketched, adding the actor parameter, a typed TASKS payload with nextNumber, and syncTasksOnPlanApproval as the one entry the approve flow calls.
Every TASKS and TASK head is read and written through ArtifactStore (write, read, childrenOf); parent is the Story id and dependencies are depends-on References.
Each create, content revision, withdraw and build round is one change log entry appended by the store; Task feedback uses the shared TASKS feedback file through the sidecar store.
updateContent returns an edited Task to draft with a new revision; apply(withdraw) withdraws a dropped Task; the TASK roll-up completes the Story from Task status.

A Task's issue is bound on the TASK head with bindArtifact; the existing tracker push creates each Task's issue under the Story's issue, and a withdrawn Task's issue is closed through the tracker port.
TASK and TASKS ids come from ArtifactIds.make and are parsed with ArtifactIds.parse.

errorCases.scenario: The plan is approved but writing the Task set fails part-way (a TASK head written, the TASKS head not, or the process stops between the plan approval and the Task creation)
errorCases.detection: syncTasksOnPlanApproval compares the TASKS head's planRevision and taskIds with the plan's rows and the TASK heads that exist (childrenOf the Story id); a TASKS head that is absent or older than the plan, or a plan row with no TASK head, is the gap
errorCases.response: createFromPlan and reconcile write the TASK heads first and the TASKS head last, and skip a head that already exists with the same content, so repeating the call finishes the job; the failure is logged and returned as { error } to the approve flow, which reports it with the approval and never fails the approval
errorCases.userImpact: The plan stays approved and the approve result names the Task set as incomplete; the next approve of the plan, or the daemon seam, finishes it

errorCases.scenario: A Task edit names order or a dependency, or tries to add or drop a Task
errorCases.detection: edit compares the patch keys with the editable set (title, summary, size, acceptanceChecks, tests) and checks that the target id is an existing TASK head
errorCases.response: Throws TaskStructureError with a message that points to re-planning the Story; nothing is written
errorCases.userImpact: The person sees why it was refused and what to do instead (run the plan workflow and approve the new plan)

errorCases.scenario: A Task edit arrives for a Task that is completed, withdrawn or superseded
errorCases.detection: edit reads the head's lifecycle status before writing
errorCases.response: Throws TaskStructureError naming the status; no write
errorCases.userImpact: A finished Task is not reopened by an edit; a person reopens it explicitly through the lifecycle first

errorCases.scenario: Two writers change the same Task at once (an edit and a reconcile, or two edits)
errorCases.detection: The store serialises writes per artifact; updateContent reads the head, compares its revision with the one the caller read, and the store raises LifecycleConflictError when they differ
errorCases.response: The second write is refused with the conflict error; the caller re-reads and retries
errorCases.userImpact: One edit lands; the other is told to retry on the new revision

errorCases.scenario: The plan's Task rows are malformed (a duplicate id, an unknown dependsOn, an order gap, a size outside S, M, L)
errorCases.detection: createFromPlan and reconcile validate the rows with the plan's own checkPlanTaskGraph before writing any head
errorCases.response: Throws TaskSetError listing the rows; nothing is written
errorCases.userImpact: The approve result shows the Task set was not made and why; the plan has to be fixed and re-approved

errorCases.scenario: A dropped Task's issue cannot be closed (offline, gh failure)
errorCases.detection: The tracker port returns a failed PortResult for the close
errorCases.response: The Task is still withdrawn; the failed close is recorded as a pending close on the TASK head's binding (pendingLink-style bookkeeping from s6) and returned in the reconcile result, and the next sync retries it
errorCases.userImpact: The Task shows withdrawn locally and its issue closes on the next sync

errorCases.scenario: A build round is recorded for a Task that has no head (a Story planned and built before s9 created Task artifacts)
errorCases.detection: recordBuildRound reads the TASK head and gets ArtifactNotFoundError
errorCases.response: The build step logs the miss and keeps writing the BUILD record's per-task result as it does today; taskBuildPassed falls back to the BUILD record only when the Task has no head
errorCases.userImpact: No change for an old Story; a new Story's Task rounds go to the Task

edgeCases.input: createFromPlan is called a second time for the same plan revision
edgeCases.expected: Nothing is written and the same TaskSet is returned

edgeCases.input: A plan with no Tasks is approved
edgeCases.expected: A TASKS head with an empty taskIds list and nextNumber 1 is written, no TASK head and no issue

edgeCases.input: A re-plan drops t2 and adds a new Task
edgeCases.expected: t2 is withdrawn, its id stays recorded in taskIds, and the new Task takes the TASKS head's nextNumber (t3 or higher), never t2

edgeCases.input: A re-plan reorders two Tasks without changing their content
edgeCases.expected: Each Task's order changes in its payload so each moves to a new revision, and the plan, not a person, made the change

edgeCases.input: A re-plan changes nothing in the Tasks
edgeCases.expected: No Task moves; the TASKS head records the new plan revision and nothing else is written

edgeCases.input: An edit whose patch equals the current content
edgeCases.expected: No revision moves, no log entry is written (an identical rewrite does not move a revision)

edgeCases.input: A Task is edited after it was approved
edgeCases.expected: It returns to draft with a new revision and needs the local user's approval again; its signoffs are not opened

edgeCases.input: A build round passes, then a later round fails
edgeCases.expected: taskBuildPassed answers from the latest round, so the Task is not complete on the earlier pass; completion is the roll-up's, recorded once

invariantsToPreserve.text: A Task id is never reused: nextNumber on the TASKS head only grows, and a withdrawn Task keeps its id in taskIds
A revision moves only when content changes; a build round, a binding write or an identical rewrite does not move it
The plan's own revision and head are never written by a Task edit or a reconcile
Heads are replaced atomically and the log entry is appended before the head, so a failure leaves a repairable gap rather than a torn Task
A plan approval is never failed by the Task set; a failure is reported beside it

migration.stateBefore: A Task is only a row in the Plan's body.tasks. Its issue record is in the Plan's meta.tracker.units and taskRefs (s6 left a two-home accessor, bindingHome and readRecord, in src/workflow/tracker/unit-issue.ts). The codec registry holds pass-through codecs for TASKS and TASK, and the sidecar store already points every TASK at its Story's TASKS log and feedback files. CompletionEvidence.taskBuildPassed reads the BUILD record's body.tasks[].passed, and a Task's build rounds are in no Task history (src/workflow/artifact-core/completion-evidence.ts, src/workflow/artifacts/plan.ts, src/workflow/tracker/unit-issue.ts).
migration.stateAfter: Approving a plan creates a TASKS head and a TASK head per plan Task, each Task with its own revision, status, log, feedback and binding; the Task unit's issue record lives on its TASK head under the Story's issue; edits go through the Task's own revision; a re-plan reconciles the set without reusing an id; a Task's build rounds are in its own log and taskBuildPassed reads them. The Plan no longer carries Task issue records.

migrationSteps.action: Type the TASK and TASKS payload codecs (replace the two pass-through bodies) and add TaskStructureError and TaskSetError; no stored data changes yet
Add the TaskSets module (createFromPlan, reconcile, edit, syncTasksOnPlanApproval, recordBuildRound) with its Task diff, number allocation and edit check; nothing calls it yet

Call syncTasksOnPlanApproval from the cli approve service before the Task push, and from the daemon's post-approval seam as a second follow-on kind, so a plan approved from either path gets its Task set

Point bindingHome and readRecord at the TASK head for a task unit, make recordUnit stop writing the Plan's units and taskRefs for a Task, and make the draft-issues hook and pushTasks resolve the Task's head before creating its issue
prerequisiteFlags: step 3 is in place, so every newly approved plan has its Task heads

migrationSteps.action: Write each build round to the Task's log from the build validate phase and make taskBuildPassed read it, with the BUILD record read only for a Task that has no head
Record the hand-offs in docs/plans/core-data-model.md: s9 creates Task heads for the stories planned before this Story and then removes the BUILD-record fallback and the Plan's Task record fields

migration.backwardCompat: A Story planned and approved before this Story has no TASKS or TASK heads, and its Task issue records are still in the Plan. Nothing rewrites them here: bindingHome answers the Plan only for a Task that has no head, and taskBuildPassed reads the BUILD record only for a Task that has no head. s9 creates the heads for those Stories and removes both fallbacks. The public surfaces (the approve result, the tracker.attach method) gain fields and a follow-on kind and lose none.

alternativesConsidered.name: A TaskSets module, run once from the approve flow, beside the tracker push
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: One new module creates the TASKS head and a TASK head per plan Task after a plan approval, reconciles a later plan revision, and handles edits; the cli approve service calls it before the Task issues are pushed.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A new src/workflow/tasks module implements sc7: createFromPlan writes the TASKS head (the ordered Task ids, the plan revision it was made from, and the next number to hand out) and one TASK head per PlanTask through ArtifactStore.write, each with parent = the Story id and a depends-on reference per dependsOn. reconcile(planId) diffs the plan's current Tasks against the TASK heads: a Task whose payload differs gets a content revision through LifecycleService.updateContent, a Task missing from the plan is withdrawn through apply(withdraw) and its issue closed, a new plan Task takes the next number from the TASKS head and is created. edit(taskId, patch, by) accepts only title/summary/size/acceptanceChecks/tests, writes through updateContent (new revision, status back to draft, no signoff), and refuses a patch that touches order or dependsOn with a message pointing to a re-plan. The cli approve service (src/cli/services/workflow.ts approve) calls createFromPlan or reconcile right after the plan approval and before autoPushTasksOnPlan, whose Task units then bind on the TASK head (bindingHome for a task unit points there). The build validate phase appends the round to the Task's log (updateAndLog with an outcome) and taskBuildPassed reads the latest round of the TASK head.
pros: One place creates and changes Tasks, so ac20 to ac23 each have one owner
Runs in the same flow that already pushes the Task issues, so the Task issue is created for a head that already exists
Uses only the store and the lifecycle service s2 and s3 built; no new write path
Task ids come from the TASKS head, so none is ever reused
cons: The daemon's workflow.approve path (approveWorkflowTarget alone) does not call the cli service, so it needs the same call or a Task set is missed
The plan approval and the Task creation are two writes: a failure between them leaves an approved plan with no Tasks until the next approve call repairs it

alternativesConsidered.name: Create the Tasks inside approveWorkflowTarget through the lifecycle service
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The Task set is created in the gate itself, in the same function that stamps the plan approval, so every approval path creates it.
alternativesConsidered.approach: approveWorkflowTarget in src/workflow/gates.ts gains a step after the plan approval is applied through the lifecycle service: with the service present it calls TaskSets.createFromPlan or reconcile. The cli approve service and the daemon handler both reach it because both call the gate. The TASK heads are written by the same service instance the gate holds, so the approval and the Tasks share one actor and one clock.
pros: Every approval path (daemon, cli, review decision) creates or reconciles the Tasks with no second call site
The approval and the Task creation are adjacent in one function, so a failure is reported in one result
cons: Puts Task creation in the gate, which s3 and s4 own; the gate gains a dependency on the new module and a second reason to change
The tracker push is outside the gate, so Task issues still have to be created later against heads the gate wrote, with the order enforced by convention
A gate that is synchronous in places (the team gate and the draft hook) would need an async seam for the creation
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Reaches every approval path with one call site, but puts a second responsibility in a gate other Stories own and needs an async seam in synchronous code.

alternativesConsidered.name: Create a Task head lazily, on first build or first edit
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A TASK head is written when something first needs it, with the plan row as the source until then.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The plan keeps the Task rows. A TASK head is created from its plan row the first time a build round, an edit or a comment sync touches that Task. The TASKS file is not written at approval.
pros: Smallest: nothing runs at plan approval, and a plan that is never built writes no Task heads
cons: Fails ac20: the Tasks do not exist together in one file at approval, and a Task has no issue, history or status until it is touched
Two sources for a Task (plan row, then head) that can disagree until the first touch
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Smallest, but fails the first criterion and leaves two sources for a Task.

alternativesConsidered.name: Keep the Tasks in the TASKS head body only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: One TASKS head holds every Task as a row with its own status and issue fields; there are no TASK heads.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The TASKS head's body carries the ordered Task rows, each with its status, revision, binding and build rounds. Edits rewrite the one head and the shared log carries per-Task entries.
pros: One file per Story, nothing to scan, and the sidecar files are already shared
cons: Fails the model: a Task would not be an Artifact with its own envelope, lifecycle, binding and history, which the HLD's sc7 and the s3 roll-up (TASK children of a STORY) already assume
Two Tasks edited at once would contend on one head, and the s3 lifecycle rules would need a second form for a row
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Breaks the model the lifecycle roll-up and sc7 already assume.

openQuestions: A Task head is written in draft status by createFromPlan (contract postcondition), but a Task whose edit 'returns to draft' and 'needs re-approval' (ac21) and whose build is admitted by the plan's approval must start approved. Resolve: after writing each head, createFromPlan applies the approve operation through LifecycleService.apply as the plan's approving actor, so a new Task is approved on the plan's approval and an edit later returns it to draft (recommended), or leave new Tasks in draft and add a separate Task approval step before build (a change to the build admission gate).

recordBuildRound is a log entry that moves no revision (a build round is not content, so k3 forbids a revision move). The store has no log-only method; the contract says it is appended to the Task's log. Resolve: append a revision-less entry with History.appendLog under ArtifactStore.exclusive, which the integrity check already skips when it looks for the log tail with a revision (recommended), or add a log-only write to ArtifactStore (a change to s2's store).

Until s9 creates Task heads for the Stories planned before this one, bindingHome falls back to the Plan's Task record and taskBuildPassed to the BUILD record for a Task with no head, which is compatibility code the Epic's no-compatibility rule discourages. Resolve: accept both fallbacks as s9-bound and record them in docs/plans/core-data-model.md for s9 to remove (recommended), or drop them and fail for a Task with no head (no Story planned before this one is still open to build).

The daemon's workflow.approve path does not run the cli approve service, so the Task set would be missed when a plan is approved there. Resolve: add a 'tasks-sync' follow-on kind to FollowOnOutcome beside s6's 'tracker-attach' and call syncTasksOnPlanApproval from the same seam at both daemon sites (recommended), or call it from approveWorkflowTarget (a change to the gate s3 and s4 own).
